title: Revisiting Luteolin Against the Mediators of Human Metastatic Colorectal Carcinoma: A Biomolecular Approach.
authors: Chakraborty, Ankita; Midde, Advaitha; Chakraborty, Pritha; Adhikary, Sourin; Kumar, Simran; Arri, Navpreet; Chandra Das, Nabarun; Sen Gupta, Parth Sarthi; Banerjee, Aditi; Mukherjee, Suprabhat
one_liner_zh: 该文研究木犀草素对结直肠癌相关蛋白的分子对接与药效筛选，虽涉及蛋白-小分子互作，但非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Metastatic colorectal carcinoma (mCRC) is one of the prevalent subtypes of human cancers and is caused by the alterations of various lifestyle and diet-associated factors. beta-catenin, GSK-3beta, PI3K-alpha, AKT1, and NF-kappaB p50 are known to be the critical regulators of tumorigenesis and immunopathogenesis of mCRC. Unfortunately, current drugs have limited efficacy, side effects and can lead to chemoresistance. Therefore, searching for a nontoxic, efficacious anti-mCRC agent is crucial and of utmost interest. The present study demonstrates the identification of a productive and nontoxic anti-mCRC agent through a five-targets (beta-catenin, GSK-3beta, PI3K-alpha, AKT1, and p50)-based and three-tier (binding affinity, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacophore) screening strategy involving a series of 30 phytocompounds having a background of anti-inflammatory/anti-mCRC efficacy alongside 5-fluorouracil (FU), a reference drug. Luteolin (a phyto-flavonoid) was eventually rendered as the most potent and safe phytocompound. This inference was verified through three rounds of validation. Firstly, luteolin was found to be effective against the different mCRC cell lines (HCT-15, HCT-116, DLD-1, and HT-29) without hampering the viability of non-tumorigenic ones (RWPE-1). Secondly, luteolin was found to curtail the clonogenicity of CRC cells, and finally, it also disrupted the formation of colospheroids, a characteristic of metastasis. While studying the mechanistic insights, luteolin was found to inhibit beta-catenin activity (a key regulator of mCRC) through direct physical interactions, promoting its degradation by activating GSK3-beta and ceasing its activation by inactivating AKT1 and PI3K-alpha. Luteolin also inhibited p50 activity, which could be useful in mitigating mCRC-associated proinflammatory milieu. In conclusion, our study provides evidence on the efficacy of luteolin against the critical key regulators of immunopathogenesis of mCRC and recommends further studies in animal models to determine the effectiveness efficacy of this natural compound for treating mCRC in the future.
abstract_zh: 转移性结直肠癌（mCRC）是人类癌症中常见的亚型之一，由多种生活方式和饮食相关因素的改变引起。已知β-catenin、GSK-3beta、PI3K-alpha、AKT1和NF-kappaB p50是mCRC肿瘤发生和免疫病理发生中的关键调控因子。遗憾的是，现有药物疗效有限、存在副作用，并可能导致化疗耐药。因此，寻找一种无毒、有效的抗mCRC药物至关重要且极具吸引力。本研究通过基于五个靶点（β-catenin、GSK-3beta、PI3K-alpha、AKT1和p50）和三层筛选策略（结合亲和力、药代动力学和药效团），对一系列30种具有抗炎/抗mCRC背景的植物化合物及参考药物5-氟尿嘧啶（FU）进行筛选，鉴定出一种有效且无毒的候选抗mCRC药物。最终，木犀草素（一种植物黄酮类化合物）被确定为最有效且安全的植物化合物。这一结论通过三轮验证得到证实。首先，木犀草素被发现对不同mCRC细胞系（HCT-15、HCT-116、DLD-1和HT-29）有效，且不影响非肿瘤细胞系（RWPE-1）的活力。其次，木犀草素被发现能抑制CRC细胞的克隆形成能力，最后，它还能破坏结肠球体（colospheroids）的形成，这是转移的一个特征。在机制研究中，木犀草素被发现通过直接物理相互作用抑制β-catenin活性（mCRC的关键调控因子），通过激活GSK3-beta促进其降解，并通过失活AKT1和PI3K-alpha终止其激活。木犀草素还抑制p50活性，这可能有助于缓解mCRC相关的促炎微环境。总之，我们的研究提供了木犀草素对mCRC免疫病理发生关键调控因子有效性的证据，并建议在动物模型中进行进一步研究，以确定这种天然化合物未来治疗mCRC的有效性。
